brief: Nomura's McElligott argues the mechanical relief-rally setup is almost too clean: NVDA beat and raised guidance, Anthropic's IPO priced above range with scarce allocations, and VIX expiry cleared without stress, leaving dealer short-gamma/vanna buying, CTA trend-reversal triggers ($7.9bn on a 2% rally, $21.1bn on 4%) and vol-control funds (up to $62.9bn) primed to buy on any vol reset. But because the trade is so obvious, everyone already owns it, which he says is itself the risk: a failed rally would mean real sellers, not cleared positioning. Goldman's Prime data shows the professional half of that bull case already happened: fundamental long/short net leverage at a 5-year low (41.6%), record tech de-grossing, momentum exposure gutted, though Goldman flags broader sentiment gauges still show no capitulation. Despite the clean quad-fecta, Nasdaq futures' 2% gain faded and the S&P slid back below its 200-day average, with AMD later plunging 11%. McElligott's test: if equities still can't rally by early next week, it signals 401(k)/real-money allocators are genuinely de-risking into bonds, not a technical squeeze.
